root_cause: The Samples job's 'Download OpenVINO artifacts (package)' step (akashchi/download-artifact) repeatedly hit GitHub Actions' internal ArtifactService ListArtifacts twirp endpoint, timing out on all 5 retry attempts over roughly a minute. This is a transient GitHub Actions infrastructure/service-side issue, not caused by the PR under test (#38731, CPU u3 weight precision support), which only touches CPU plugin source and test files unrelated to CI artifact handling. The subsequent DNS resolution failure ('Could not resolve host: github.com') during post-job git submodule cleanup on the same runner is a secondary symptom of the same underlying runner/network connectivity degradation, not an independent root cause. This is the third occurrence of the identical ArtifactService timeout signature within about an hour on this repository's post-commit pipeline, indicating an ongoing GitHub-side availability or networking issue affecting hosted runners rather than a one-off blip.
reproduction_steps: N/A - not reproducible locally; this is a transient GitHub Actions service-side (ArtifactService) timeout and hosted-runner DNS resolution issue, not a code or test defect.
recommended_actions: No code changes needed for PR #38731 - the failure is unrelated to the merged change.
Re-run the failed 'Samples / Samples' job; ArtifactService timeouts are typically transient and succeed on retry.

If this signature recurs frequently (this is the 3rd time within ~1 hour), consider filing a GitHub Support ticket referencing elevated ArtifactService latency for openvinotoolkit/openvino, and/or increasing the download-artifact action's retry count/backoff as a mitigation.
Monitor the actions/upload-artifact and akashchi/download-artifact action versions in use for known reliability issues with large artifacts on Azure westus3 hosted runners.
prevention_strategies: Add resilience by wrapping the artifact download step with an explicit workflow-level retry (e.g., a composite action or nick-fields/retry wrapper) so transient ArtifactService timeouts do not fail the whole job immediately. Consider adding step-level `continue-on-error` plus a conditional re-download step, or splitting large package artifacts into smaller chunks to reduce the chance of ListArtifacts timing out under service load. AI Team Self-Improvement: when a post-commit CI failure log shows 'Request timeout: /twirp/github.actions.results.api.v1.ArtifactService/ListArtifacts' or 'Could not resolve host: github.com' with no code/test changes implicated, immediately classify as Network/Infrastructure (GitHub-side transient issue) and do not scan the PR diff for a code root cause - recommend a job re-run instead of a code fix.
historical_context: This exact ArtifactService ListArtifacts timeout signature (pattern 77303b969eadbc6a) has now been recorded 3 times within roughly 1 hour on 2026-10-30 (runs 41003290355 at 05:58, 41005296042 at 06:36, and this run 41013943699 at 06:58), all post-commit, all on different jobs downloading the openvino_package artifact. A separate but related DNS resolution failure signature (pattern eeae3ce3f5218e80, 'Could not resolve host: github.com') was previously seen once on 2026-10-13. The clustering of 3 ArtifactService timeouts in under an hour strongly suggests an ongoing GitHub Actions service degradation window rather than independent flakiness.
